content:
Bug report: `reply.removeHeader()` does not remove headers that were set on the raw
response.

Plugins and compatibility layers often set headers directly on the Node.js response,
e.g. `reply.raw.setHeader('X-Powered-By', 'legacy')`. Fastify's reply sees those
headers: `reply.getHeader('x-powered-by')` returns `'legacy'` and
`reply.hasHeader('x-powered-by')` is `true`. But

    reply.removeHeader('X-Powered-By')

has no effect on them: `getHeader` / `hasHeader` still report the header and it is
still sent to the client.

Expected behavior: after `reply.removeHeader(name)`, the header is gone, whether it
was set through `reply.header()` or directly on `reply.raw`. It is no longer reported
by `reply.getHeader()`, `reply.getHeaders()` or `reply.hasHeader()`, and it is not
sent in the response. Header names are case-insensitive, as everywhere else in the
reply API.

`reply.removeHeader()` now also removes headers that were set directly on `reply.raw`, so they no longer show up in `getHeader`, `getHeaders` or `hasHeader` and are not sent. The new test passes along with the existing unit tests (2049 pass, 0 fail), and eslint is clean on the changed files. I did not run the full `scripts/check.sh` (type tests included).

The fix is in `lib/reply.js`. After deleting the header from the reply's own header map, it calls `this.raw.removeHeader()` with the lowercased name, so case doesn't matter. The raw removal is skipped once headers have been sent, because Node throws in that case.

I added a test to `test/internals/reply.test.js` that sets `X-Powered-By` on the raw response, removes it with mixed-case names, and checks the header is gone from the getters and from the response. It also checks that another raw header is left alone.
